content.text:
I've submitted index 17 (Bi 0.20 / Cu 0.80) as the best composition. It's only the least bad: all three merit measurements gave negative (cathodic) photocurrent, so no measured composition worked as a photoanode.

| Index | Bi / Cu | Photocurrent (A) | Why I measured it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | 0.67 / 0.33 | −9.9e-7 | CuBi2O4 (a Bi–Cu oxide compound) is predicted stable here |
| 7 | 0.83 / 0.17 | −4.4e-7 | The Bi-rich end, where n-type Bi2O3 might give anodic current |
| 17 | 0.20 / 0.80 | −1.6e-7 | The only unexplored region, and the model's suggestion |

- **Model checks:** MACE puts CuBi2O4 on the convex hull, meaning it's predicted stable. MEGNet predicts a near-zero band gap for it, which I disregarded because the known experimental gap is about 1.5–1.8 eV. MEGNet gives Bi2O3 a 2.34 eV gap, below the 2.72 eV photon energy, so it should absorb.
- **Pattern:** negative current across the whole range fits p-type copper-containing oxides. The current was strongest at CuBi2O4 and weakest at the Cu-rich end.
- **Not done:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so the phases in these films were never confirmed. The 15 unmeasured compositions, including the middle of the range between Bi 0.2 and 0.6, earn nothing even if one of them is anodic.
